questions.stem: Suppose your university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on future applications of robots on campus. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Robots are no longer figures from science fiction; in the near future, they are likely to become common helpers on university campuses. As the university newspaper invites students to imagine future applications of robots on campus, I believe intelligent machines will mainly reshape our campus life in three areas: library services, laboratory assistance, and daily guidance.

First, in the library, robots could locate, fetch, and even deliver requested books to reading rooms, saving students valuable study time. Second, in science labs, robotic assistants might handle repetitive experiments or dangerous chemicals, allowing students to focus on analysis and innovation. Third, robots placed around the campus could provide real-time directions and campus information for visitors and freshmen, reducing confusion during busy periods.

Of course, these technologies should serve people rather than replace human interaction. If universities introduce robots wisely, campus life will become more efficient, safe, and welcoming.

transcript.text: 1 A 104-year-old woman is selling the house she has lived in since she was two years old.
Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War, and spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street.
She is now putting it on the market, having lived in it through the Second World War and the invention of television. 2 Her family bought the house for £200 in 1921.
And it is now priced at some £170,000.
According to the Bank of England's inflation calculator, £200 in 1921 would be worth £7,750 today.
According to the estate agent, the house was built in 1882 and originally featured a well for the entire road.
Except for some changes in the toilet and wash area, much of the house remains the same.
Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health.

questions.stem: What does the news report say about Nancy Gifford?

options.text: She was born months after the end of World War I.
She has been living in her house throughout her life.
She suffered a great deal during the Second World War.
She is a 102-year-old woman living in Somerset Village.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War, and spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street.信号：首段人物定义句 。新闻首段在抛出事件（104岁老妇卖房）后，用 Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War 给出人物关键身份信…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：原文说 the house she has lived in since she was two years old，并非一生都在此居住；She has been living in her house throughout her life. 把起点从两岁偷换为'一生'。 借用原文：having lived in it through the Second World War
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：原文仅说 having lived in it through the Second World War，表示她经历了二战，但并未说她 suffered a great deal；She suffered a great deal during the Second World War. 把'经历'强改为'遭受巨大痛苦'。 借用原文：A 104-year-old woman
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：原文说 Nancy Gifford 是 A 104-year-old woman，且 spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street；She is a 102-year-old woman living in Somerset Village. 把居住时长误植为年龄，同时把 Somerset Village of Street 简化为 Somerset Village。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War ↔ She was born months after the end of World War I. 同义替换：the First World War = World War I）

questions.evidenceText: Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War, and spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street.

questions.stem: Why is Mrs. Gifford selling the house?

options.text: She has been persuaded by the estate agent.
She needs the money badly for her health.
She is moving to a nursing home.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Mrs. Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health.信号：because of 因果信号 。答案句以 because of her health 结尾，直接回答 Why；卖房与搬去养老院是并列结果，健康才是原因。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：原文 According to the estate agent, the house was built in 1882... 只说明中介提供了房屋信息，并未说 Mrs. Gifford 是被中介说服卖房；She has been persuaded by the estate agent. 把'中介存在'曲解为'被中介说服'。 借用原文：because of her health
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：原文 because of her health 说明健康是原因，但并未说她 needs the money badly；She needs the money badly for her health. 把'因健康搬家'偷换成'因健康急需钱'。 借用原文：moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：原文说 moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury，即她要搬去格拉斯顿伯里；She is leaving Glastonbury Village. 把'搬入附近格拉斯顿伯里'说成'离开格拉斯顿伯里'，方向相反。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Mrs. Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health ↔ She is moving to a nursing home. 因果同构：卖房是为搬去养老院）

questions.evidenceText: Mrs. Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health.

transcript.text: 1 The navy rescued a man who survived 24 days floating in the sea on a boat by eating tomato sauce and vegetable powder.

The man, 47, wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue. 2 The man told authorities that his experience began in December when currents swept the sailboat out to sea while he was making repairs.
To survive, the man collected rainwater with a cloth.
He had to constantly remove water from the boat to prevent it from sinking.
He also tried to light a fire to send a distress signal without success.
Finally, a plane passed by and he signaled with a mirror.
He said the navy told him that he was spotted when the plane passed again.
The sailboat was abandoned at sea when the man was picked up by a nearby merchant ship.
He was found in good health but had lost weight.

questions.stem: What does the news report say was key to the man's rescue?

options.text: The word HELP written on the boat.
His use of a mirror to send a signal.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The man, 47, wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue.信号：非限制性定语从句 'which was key to his rescue' 直接点题 。which was key to his rescue 把前文的 'wrote the word "HELP" in Engl…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：The navy's timely arrival 中的 navy 确实出现在录音中，但原文只说 The navy rescued a man，海军是执行救援的一方，而非 'key to his rescue' 所指的原因。 借用原文：he signaled with a mirror
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：His rich sailing experience 中的 sailing experience 在整段录音中没有任何对应信息，属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：His use of a mirror to send a signal 中的 mirror 确实在 he signaled with a mirror 中出现，但这是男子在飞机经过时的求救尝试；原文明确说 key 是 HELP，镜子只是另一条求生手段。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat ↔ The word HELP written on the boat 动作名词化 + 核心信息保留）

questions.evidenceText: The man, 47, wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man when he was rescued?

options.text: He was too distressed to pick himself up.
He entirely abandoned himself to despair.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：He was found in good health but had lost weight.信号：新闻结尾总结人物状态的收束句 。He was found in good health 中的 was found 是被救后的总结性动词，in good health 直接回应题干 'when he was rescu…

optionAnalysis.A: 偷换概念：He lost all consciousness 中的 lost 可能让考生联想到 had lost weight，但 weight 与 consciousness 是完全不同的概念，属于偷换概念。 借用原文：The sailboat was abandoned at sea
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：He was too distressed to pick himself up 中的 distressed 与 pick himself up 在录音中均未出现，且与 'in good health' 的正面评价相反。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：He entirely abandoned himself to despair 中的 abandoned 可能让考生联想到 The sailboat was abandoned at sea，但原文主语是 sailboat（船被遗弃），选项却把它改成 He abandoned himself（自暴自弃），且 despair 在录音中从未出现。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（in good health ↔ He was in good condition 近义形容词替换）

questions.evidenceText: He was found in good health but had lost weight.

transcript.text: 1 The board of Denver public schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment.

The specific schools will be announced in the coming days, a district spokesperson said. 2 The school board approved criteria to close schools with fewer than 215 students, as well as schools with fewer than 275 students and a projected decline in enrollment.
In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said.
"3,000 students may not seem like that many students, but to a budget where you're receiving per-pupil funding, that's about 36 million dollars," district spokesperson Scott Pribble said.
"We know that there are impacts and it's heartbreaking and difficult work.
But in order for the district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said.
The district said the decreased budget means it cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services or specialized programming to schools with lower enrollment.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the elementary and middle schools to be closed in Denver?

options.text: Their efforts to provide social services have been ignored.
They have been criticized by the Denver school board.
They have taken various steps to get more funding.
Their enrollment has been on a noticeable decline.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The board of Denver public schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment.信号：因果信号 caused by 。答案句中 caused by declining enrollment 直接给出关闭学校的 causal chain：预算减少 ← 入学下降 ← 学校关闭。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 A 说‘提供社会服务的努力被忽视’，但录音末句只说 cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services，是预算不足导致无法提供，并非努力被忽视；social services 这个词录音确实念到了，但语义与选项不符。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：选项 B 说学校被校董会批评，但录音中校董会是作出关闭决定的主体，并未出现 criticized 的语义，属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 选项 C 说学校采取各种措施争取资金，但录音讲的是‘因预算减少而关校’，没有提到学校主动 steps to get more funding，属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（declining enrollment ↔ Their enrollment has been on a noticeable decline. 同义替换 declining = on a noticeable decline）

questions.evidenceText: The board of Denver public schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment.

questions.stem: What does the Denver district expect to do in the next three years?

options.text: Approve criteria for closing schools with decreased funding.
Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students.
Decide which elementary and middle schools to close.
Alter its per-pupil funding policy on a rational basis.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said.信号：时间信号 + 数字信号 。答案句中 In the next three years 与 expects to enroll 3,000 fewer 形成时间与数字的双重信号，直接对应题干。

optionAnalysis.A: 选项 A 说‘批准关闭标准’，但录音中 The school board approved criteria 用一般过去时，表示已经批准，不是 expect to do 的未来动作。 借用原文：The specific schools will be announced in the coming days
optionAnalysis.C: 答非所问：选项 C 说‘决定关闭哪些中小学’，但录音中 The specific schools will be announced in the coming days 指近期宣布，不是 in the next three years 的预期动作；属于答非所问。 借用原文：per-pupil funding
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：选项 D 说‘改变 per-pupil funding 政策’，但录音只是用 per-pupil funding 解释预算计算方式，并未说要 alter policy，属于偷换概念。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students ↔ Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students. 原词复现）

questions.evidenceText: In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said.

questions.stem: Why are some schools in Denver to be closed according to the district spokesperson?

options.text: To enable the district to remain competitive.
To avoid a negative impact on its economy.
To keep the district free of debt.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）："We know that there are impacts and it's heartbreaking and difficult work. But in order for the district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said.信号：目的信号 in order for... to stay out of debt 。发言人先用 But 转折，再用 in order for the district to stay out of debt 点明关闭…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：选项 A 说‘让学区保持竞争力’，但录音全文未出现 competitive / competition 等词，属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 B 说‘避免对经济造成负面影响’，但录音中 there are impacts 是承认影响存在，并未说 avoid negative impact on its economy；impact 原词出现，但语义被扭曲。 借用原文：decreased budget
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 D 说‘为了获得预期资金’，但录音讲的是预算减少、按 per-pupil funding 计算缺口，关闭学校是为了 stay out of debt（减少支出/避免负债），而不是 obtain funding（获得资金）；funding 原词出现，但目的被替换。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（stay out of debt ↔ To keep the district free of debt. 同义替换 stay out of = keep... free of）

questions.evidenceText: "We know that there are impacts and it's heartbreaking and difficult work. But in order for the district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said.

transcript.text: M: Good afternoon, Theatre Bookings International. My name's Philip. How may I help you today?
transcript.zh: M: 下午好，这里是国际剧院订票中心。我叫菲利普。今天有什么可以帮您的吗？

transcript.text: W: Oh, good afternoon. My name's Helen. I've been trying to book tickets for the musical Cats in London on the evening of May the 28th, but I can't get the computer to accept my card payment. I've tried three times, but it just doesn't want to take it.
transcript.zh: W: 哦，下午好。我叫海伦。我一直想预订5月28日晚上在伦敦观看音乐剧《猫》的票，但电脑就是不接受我的信用卡付款。我已经试了三次，可它就是不肯接受。

transcript.text: M: That's OK, madam. I can book it and take the payment over the phone if that's not a problem for you.
transcript.zh: M: 没关系，女士。如果您不介意的话，我可以帮您预订，并通过电话收取票款。

transcript.text: W: That would be wonderful. I'm not very good with computers. My husband usually does all of these things, but he is in Italy on a business trip until next Thursday, and I know how quickly these things can sell out.

transcript.text: W: Yes, that's the one, and I will need two tickets please, not too close to the front.
transcript.zh: W: 是的，就是那场。我需要两张票，谢谢，位置不要离前排太近。

transcript.text: M: Actually, all the tickets at the front are already sold out anyway. But I can offer you two upstairs near the middle. I assume that you don't want to be too high up.
transcript.zh: M: 实际上，前排的票已经全部售罄了。不过我可以给您安排楼上的两张票，位置靠近中间。我想您应该不想坐得太高吧。

transcript.text: W: Oh, my goodness, no. I'm scared of heights, and you can never see anything if you are too high up anyway.
transcript.zh: W: 哦，天哪，当然不想。我恐高，而且坐得太高的话，反正什么也看不清。

transcript.text: M: No problem, madam. I'll reserve those for you now, and all we need after that is the details of your card number and your full name, and then we are done.
transcript.zh: M: 没问题，女士。我现在就为您预留那两个座位，之后我们只需要您的卡号和全名，办完这些就可以了。

transcript.text: 1 If U.S. workers want to switch jobs, they'd better do it now.
Last year, job switchers earned far higher wage increases than those staying in their jobs.
But the gap is now closing.

A three-month moving average of annual wage increases from the Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank's Wage Tracker shows that U.S. job switchers got the highest wage increase last July, when the measure touched 8.5%.
Since then, it has gone up and down, and has been going steadily down since November.
The gap in wage gains between people who switched jobs and those who stayed in their jobs is now closing.
On average, people who changed jobs have almost always gotten better pay raises than those who stayed.
But in the past, the difference was usually around one percentage point.
In July though, the gap widened to 2.6 percentage points. 2 But now wage growth is slowing down for everyone, and job switchers are getting smaller wage bumps in their new jobs.
At the moment, those who change jobs get an average 7.3% raise every year, while those who stay get a 5.4% raise.
That suggests the demand for workers has reached, or is at least nearing, its peak.
The labor market is likely cooling, because even a shortage of workers isn't overcoming the historic imbalance between employers and employees in the U.S.
The volume of income that workers take home as a proportion of what the U.S. economy produces is still falling.

transcript.text: 1 Highly processed foods—the kinds made with lots of sugar, fat and salt—make up as much as 60% of the average American diet.
But a new study shows that their low price and convenience come at a cost to health.
The study found that when people ate a highly processed diet, they consumed about 500 more calories per day than they did when they ate a less processed diet.

They also gained two pounds over two weeks, even though both diets had the same amounts of nutrients, like sugar, fat, fiber and salt. 2 It wasn't a shock to find highly processed foods weren't healthy; other research has linked them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity.
What was unexpected was that sugar, fat and salt didn't seem to be what caused people to overeat.
This is the first trial that demonstrates that there is something about highly processed foods—independent of those nutrients—that causes people to overeat.
The study also found that, when eating a highly processed diet, people ate faster.
This could be one reason why they gained more weight.
Highly processed food tends to be softer, which makes it easier to chew and swallow.
One theory is that if you're eating more quickly, you're not giving your guts enough time to signal to your brain that you've had enough calories and that you're full.
By the time the brain gets that signal, you've already overeaten.

transcript.text: 1 Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house.
This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values.

But new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females. 2 The new study looked at how men and women were dividing work at home and why they divided it that way.
In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked.
For example, men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women.
They leaned toward wanting primary responsibility for such tasks.
The researchers stated that differences in enjoyment of household and childcare tasks matched how men and women chose to split tasks.
The researchers added that there was not a single childcare task that men liked more than women.
Keep in mind, however, that, as with any research on group differences, there were large within-group differences.
The study's authors concluded that differences in men's and women's time spent on childcare and household tasks do not mean dissatisfaction.
The authors noted that previous research revealed gender differences in attitudes towards family and career.
These differences appear as early as six years old.
Girls that age already show more interest in helping and caring for others than boys do, and they already exhibit a greater orientation toward family versus career.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: If this doesn't encourage you to squeeze in a workout today, nothing will: a new study from Sweden shows that women who were highly fit in mid-life were nearly 90% less likely to get dementia(失智) decades later.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: After initial exercise tests in middle age, researchers followed the women for 44 years. Both groups lived just as long, but those who could ride an exercise bike at a fast rate for 6 minutes in the initial test had a much lower risk of dementia later on than those who couldn't complete the workout.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The study, published Wednesday in the journal Neurology, couldn't prove that exercise prevented dementia, and the findings aren't a surprise—it's long been known there's a correlation between exercise and decreased dementia risk—but the results were particularly dramatic. About 5% of the women with the highest peak workload—those who were able to bike the hardest over those 6 minutes—developed dementia, compared to 25% of those with medium fitness and 45% who weren't fit enough to finish the test, the study found. Overall, women who were highly fit compared to those who were moderately fit decreased their risk of dementia by 88%. The few highly fit women who did develop dementia became symptomatic at age 90 on average, 11 years later than the moderately fit.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: "I'm very surprised that the finding was so strong," said Ingmar Skoog, the paper's senior author and a psychiatry(精神病学) professor at The University of Gothenburg in Sweden. "It really shows the importance of exercise."

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Dementia, as defined in medical dictionaries, is a broad term that describes a loss of thinking ability, memory, attention, logical reasoning, and other mental abilities. These changes are severe enough to interfere with social or occupational functioning. Dementia isn't a disease. Instead, it's a group of symptoms caused by other conditions. It happens when the parts of your brain used for learning, memory, decision making, and language are damaged or diseased. About 5%-8% of adults over age 65 have some form of dementia. This percentage doubles every 5 years after 65. As many as half of people in their 80s have some form of dementia.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Dementia is not temporary confusion or forgetfulness that might result from an infection that heals without treatment. It can also come from an underlying(潜在的) illness or side effects of medications. Dementia typically gets worse over time. People with dementia have problems with thinking and remembering that affect their ability to manage their daily life.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Dementia is typically associated with declines in cognitive function. Yet researchers have found an association between dementia and declines in hearing and other basic sensory functions.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Though the study mentioned above was fairly small (only 191 women took the initial fitness test, which means it's hard to maintain statistical significance while breaking the group down into sub-categories of more or less fit), it does give us hope that dementia can be prevented or delayed through exercise in one's middle age.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Alzheimer's(阿尔茨海默症) and other dementias are believed to begin 15-20 years before symptoms even appear, so it makes sense that exercising in mid-life would affect the risk, Skoog said. Exercise alone is not likely to prevent Alzheimer's, but the study shows people are not helpless in the face of one of the most feared, costliest and common diseases of old age, he added. And the same activities that help prevent Alzheimer's—including avoiding smoking, getting adequate exercise and sleep and eating a healthy diet—also prevent heart disease, he said, making them even more worthwhile. "You can do something yourself to decrease your odds," Skoog said.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Maintaining a healthy lifestyle in mid-life, decades before disease sets in, makes sense, said David Knopman, a fellow of the American Academy of Neurology, who was not involved in the study. "I suspect it's a dose," said Knopman, also associate director of the Alzheimer's Disease Research Center at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. "Starting in late life is better than not starting at all, but starting in mid-life seems to offer a larger benefit."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Although it is not entirely clear why exercise helps put off or prevent Alzheimer's, Knopman said it's likely that exercise maintains good blood flow to the brain. "When the brain is healthier from a vascular(血管的) point of view, it can absorb more Alzheimer's pathogen(病原体) before people become symptomatic," he said.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: The message isn't that everyone needs to run marathons in middle age, Knopman said, but a healthy lifestyle pays off.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: This type of study can't say exactly what kind of exercise is best, or how much is needed—only a study that has a placebo(安慰剂) group and tracks people going forward can do that, said Keith Fargo, director of scientific programs and outreach at the non-profit Alzheimer's Association. "The literature has not yet settled on an amount or type of exercise that is going to be key, although the bulk of literature has suggested that aerobic(有氧的) exercise is what you need to be doing," he said. That doesn't mean you have to compete in marathons but "more than a 10-min dog walk" would be a good idea, Fargo said.

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: Several lifestyle studies are getting underway soon, including one backed by the Alzheimer's Association called the US POINTER study, which will offer at-risk adults, ages 60-79, a series of lifestyle interventions(干预) to see if they impact Alzheimer's risk. That and other Alzheimer's-related studies are always looking for volunteers to participate, he said.

paragraphs.label: O
paragraphs.text: In the next three to five years, these studies should allow researchers to provide clearer recommendations for exercise and other lifestyle modifications that might reduce Alzheimer's risk, such as sleep, diet and social activities, Fargo said. But it's already quite clear that exercising at any point in life is better for your brain than not exercising at all, Fargo added.

paragraphs.label: P
paragraphs.text: "If you don't want to have dementia when you're 80, the time to start getting fit is now," he said. "It may not necessarily give you a longer life, but there's a compelling body of work that it will give you more good years."

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance. They were then asked why they think they did so well.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; "penta-" meaning 5, and "tonic" meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other.

paragraphs.text: There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.

Dining etiquette is an important part of traditional Chinese culture, embodying the warm and courteous way of treating guests.
